prediction.clinical_reasoning: The patient's chief complaint includes abdominal pain and bloating, as well as swelling of the abdomen and extremities. The patient also reports infrequent bowel movements and difficulty digesting food properly. Based on these symptoms, a possible primary diagnosis is Celiac disease. Secondary diagnoses could include Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS) or Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD). To confirm the diagnosis, recommended tests include blood tests for antibodies associated with celiac disease, such as anti-endomysial antibody test and anti-tissue transglutaminase antibody test. Additionally, an endoscopy may be performed to evaluate the small intestine for damage characteristic of celiac disease.
